transcript:
Header: 2025-06-03 09:32 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Daniel (ML Eng), Aisha (Lead SRE), Tom (CTO)

Summary: quick sync on quantization experiments (INT8 vs FP8). Share results, dig into outliers, plan next runs and Dedicated pool benchmark.

[00:00] Maya: hey team, thanks for joining, quick agenda - results recap, a few odd failing prompts, then next steps.
[00:18] Daniel: yeah, thanks, we got the last artifact, ran the 2k eval you sent. overall looks promising, but a handful of safety-related prompts flipped.
[00:33] Liam: right, our INT8 run (per your baseline) showed about 30 to 35 percent throughput increase on A100-80 with static per-tensor quant, latency median down from ~180ms to ~120ms for 512 tokens; tail still a bit variable.
[00:50] Aisha: when you say tail, like p95/p99?
[00:55] Liam: p95 down from 340 to 210, p99 improved but we saw some spikes around long context where KV cache hits interact with quant noise.
[01:10] Tom: and what's FP8 look like? we were curious because the vendor paper promised even more gains.
[01:16] Maya: FP8 gives another 10-15% perf on top of INT8 numbers in our microbench, so roughly 40-50% over FP16 baseline, but we're seeing stability issues on certain prompt patterns and outlier layers that blow up.
[01:34] Daniel: can you explain the outlier layers? are those like attention projection layers?
[01:39] Liam: yeah mostly attention q/k/v and some first feedforward layers. the dynamic range there occasionally exceeds calibration, causing quantization overflow and very bad tokens. we added per-channel clipping and it helped reduce the flips.
[01:56] Aisha: how bad are the quality regressions overall? numbers please.
[02:01] Maya: quick numbers from the 2k eval: semantic-similarity pass rate 98.9% FP16->INT8 (so ~1.1% drop), for FP8 it's 98.2% (~1.8% drop). generation coherence metric dropped ~0.6% for INT8, ~1.4% for FP8.
[02:21] Daniel: so small but not negligible. The safety flips concern me because they could be showstoppers.
[02:28] Liam: agreed. for safety-sensitive prompts we recommend config-level routing - keep those on FP16 or fall back to FP16. We can also add per-prompt score thresholding to trigger fallbacks.
[02:42] Tom: what about cost savings - how do these map to dollars?
[02:46] Maya: rough delta: INT8 reduces GPU time per token by ~30% so ~30-35% cost saving on token compute; FP8 we estimate 40-45% but with caveats. depending on your Dedicated pricing that could move the needle materially.
[03:03] Daniel: note that our main use case is document summarization + QA with PII redaction. any change to generation quality that affects redaction is unacceptable.
[03:14] Maya: totally. that's why the plan is A/B with fallback; keep anything tagged high-sensitivity pinned to FP16/FP32.
[03:22] Liam: technical note - we saw improved KV cache memory footprint with INT8 so larger batch sizes possible. For Stratus's average sequence length we measured batching improved throughput by ~2.1x vs baseline when using INT8 optimized kernels.
[03:40] Aisha: about the calibration - the repo had per-layer calibration scripts, do those need customer data to calibrate?
[03:47] Liam: good q - you can run calibration with representative unlabeled text; for best results use ~10-20k tokens sampled from your corpus. we included a small script to sample and run calibration; if you want we can run it on your side or run it here with your sample.
[04:03] Daniel: we'll run it first on our side, don't want to share PII.
[04:07] Maya: perfect. we'll share step-by-step.
[04:11] Tom: curious about per-layer mixed precision - can we keep critical layers in FP16 and quantize others?
[04:17] Liam: yes hybrid schemes are supported; we actually shipped a per-layer override in the config. that fixed most of the failing prompts in our internal tests.
[04:28] Daniel: any changes needed in the inference runtime? or is this just config and existing kernels?
[04:33] Liam: most is config but we did enable a few INT8-specific kernels and small jit patches; in Redwood Hosted it's behind an opt-in flag, in Dedicated we can pre-provision images with the kernels enabled.
[04:45] Maya: to be crystal, our recommended path: run INT8 with per-layer overrides, run 10k eval, if FP8 shows acceptable stability then try canary in Dedicated for 24h on a subset of traffic.
[05:00] Aisha: about monitoring - what metrics should we track to detect regressions quickly?
[05:05] Liam: track semantic similarity distribution, token-level log-prob differences, and a safety-flip counter. Also keep latency p95/p99 and error rates. We'll provide dashboard queries for Console.
[05:18] Daniel: we saw a few hallucination cases in FP8 where facts were hallucinated - did you see that too?
[05:24] Liam: yes, seems correlated with outlier quantization in FF layers; clipping + per-channel scaling reduced hallucinations in our tests.
[05:34] Tom: are there any known incompatibilities with your Dedicated infra, like certain drivers or cuda versions?
[05:39] Maya: we document driver compatibility; for FP8 especially we need a newer CUDA+cuBLAS build - we'll share exact build matrix. For A100 we recommend driver X.Y and runtime Z.
[05:51] Aisha: when you say spikes with long context, can you be more specific - is it because of KV growth or something else?
[05:58] Liam: partly KV growth, partly accumulation of quant noise across many self-attention steps. We mitigated by using periodic re-calibration for very long sessions and sticky FP16 for certain early layers.
[06:14] Daniel: ok. for the 2k eval we ran, I can share the sample prompt IDs where flips occurred.
[06:19] Maya: please do, that will let us triage faster.
[06:22] Daniel: I'll upload to the shared bucket after this call.
[06:26] Liam: one more note on perf - INT8 improved packing efficiency so your cost per 1M tokens drops roughly 30%; one caveat is GPU utilization patterns change, so scheduler tuning in Dedicated can further improve numbers.
[06:40] Tom: any concerns about encryption or KMS when using Dedicated with quant kernels?
[06:45] Maya: no, quantization doesn't change data-at-rest or key management. We'll integrate with your KMS as usual; logs/audit stays the same.
[06:54] Aisha: do you have sample dashboards? we'd like alerts for safety-flip > 0.1% over baseline.
[06:59] Liam: yup we'll provide dashboard templates and alert rules; we'll drop them in the shared folder.
[07:05] Maya: timeline check - we propose: share quant config by 6/5, customer runs 10k eval by 6/12, Dedicated benchmark 6/10 (tentative), then review next week. ok?
[07:17] Daniel: yes, that works.
[07:19] Tom: one last ask - can you annotate which prompts are high-sensitivity so we can auto-route?
[07:25] Maya: we can provide an example classifier and rule set for tagging.
[07:29] Aisha: good. also we need a short risk doc summarizing FP8 caveats for leadership.
[07:34] Maya: will do.
[07:36] Liam: action items recap: I'll send runbook and per-layer notes; Maya will share config; Daniel/Aisha run eval and provision Dedicated access.
[07:46] Daniel: thanks, I'm going to upload the failing prompt IDs now.
[07:49] Maya: perfect, thanks all. we'll follow up in email and the shared drive.
